parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
Anhydrous barium chloride can be obtained from the hydrated salt, as shown in reaction 1.
reaction 1 $$\text{BaCl}_2\cdot2\text{H}_2\text{O(s)} + 2\text{SOCl}_2\text{(l)} \rightarrow \text{BaCl}_2\text{(s)} + 2\text{SO}_2\text{(g)} + 4\text{HCl(g)}$$
parts.text: Describe **one** observation when reaction 1 is carried out.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
The entropy change, $\Delta S^\ominus$, for reaction 1 at $25^\circ\text{C}$ is $+768\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Explain why $\Delta S^\ominus$ has a large positive value.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
Table 2.1 shows the enthalpy changes of formation, $\Delta H_\text{f}^\ominus$, for the compounds in reaction 1.

Table 2.1

| compound | $\Delta H_\text{f}^\ominus/\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{BaCl}_2\text{(s)}$ | $-859$ |
| $\text{BaCl}_2\cdot2\text{H}_2\text{O(s)}$ | $-1460$ |
| $\text{SOCl}_2\text{(l)}$ | $-246$ |
| $\text{SO}_2\text{(g)}$ | $-297$ |
| $\text{HCl(g)}$ | $-92$ |

Calculate the standard Gibbs free energy change, $\Delta G^\ominus$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, for reaction 1 at $25^\circ\text{C}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: When aqueous solutions of $\text{BaCl}_2$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ are mixed, a yellow precipitate of $\text{BaCrO}_4\text{(s)}$ is produced and an acidic solution remains.
parts.text: Write the ionic equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Barium sulfate is the least soluble of the Group 2 sulfates.
parts.text: Explain the trend in the solubilities of the Group 2 sulfates.
